text.en: Master all 12 tenses with one story-based system. No more confusion between Present Perfect and Past Simple — ever again!
text.hi: All 12 tenses ko ek story-based system se master karo. Present Perfect aur Past Simple mein confusion hamesha ke liye khatam!

content.en:
🎬 The Whole System in One Story (Read this first!)

Forget memorising 12 separate rules. Think of it like a cricket match being filmed:

3 Time Zones — Present (aaj ka match), Past (kal ka match), Future (kal ka match)

4 Camera Angles on EVERY time zone:
1. Simple → Wide shot. Just the fact. "He scored."
2. Continuous → Zoomed-in, action happening live. "He is scoring / was scoring / will be scoring."
3. Perfect → Camera cuts to AFTER the action — showing the result. "He has scored / had scored / will have scored."
4. Perfect Continuous → Shows the action running for a stretch of time, still relevant now. "He has been scoring / had been scoring / will have been scoring."

That's it. Every one of the 12 tenses is just (1 of 3 time zones) + (1 of 4 camera angles). Once this clicks, you're not memorising 12 things — you're memorising 1 system.
content.hi:
🎬 Pura System Ek Story Mein (Pehle Ye Padho!)

12 alag rules yaad karna chhodo. Isko ek cricket match film ho raha hai ki tarah socho:

3 Time Zones — Present (aaj ka match), Past (kal ka match), Future (kal ka match)

Har time zone pe 4 Camera Angles:
1. Simple → Wide shot. Bas fact. "He scored."
2. Continuous → Zoomed-in, action live ho raha hai. "He is scoring / was scoring / will be scoring."
3. Perfect → Camera action ke BAAD cut hota hai — result dikhata hai. "He has scored / had scored / will have scored."
4. Perfect Continuous → Action ek time period tak chal raha hai, abhi bhi relevant hai. "He has been scoring / had been scoring / will have been scoring."

Bas itna hi. 12 tenses mein se har ek sirf (3 time zones mein se 1) + (4 camera angles mein se 1) hai. Ye click hote hi, tum 12 cheezein yaad nahi kar rahe — tum 1 system yaad kar rahe ho.

content.en:
The Secret Formula

Every tense follows: Subject + Helping Verb + Main Verb + Object

Helping Verbs:
• Present → do/does/is/am/are/have/has
• Past → did/was/were/had
• Future → will/shall

After EVERY modal → always V1 (base form)

content.en:
Present Tense (4 Types) — with real examples

1. Simple Present → S + V1(s/es) + O
Keywords: always, usually, often, every day
Example: Papa checks his phone first thing every morning.

2. Present Continuous → S + am/is/are + V1+ing + O
Keywords: now, at the moment, currently
Example: Relax, I am watching the match right now, will call you after.

3. Present Perfect → S + have/has + V3 + O
Keywords: just, already, yet, ever, never, since, for
Example: Bro, I have already submitted the assignment — chill.

4. Present Perfect Continuous → S + have/has + been + V1+ing + O
Keywords: since (point of time), for (duration)
Example: She has been preparing for boards for three months now.

content.en:
Past Tense (4 Types) — with real examples

1. Simple Past → S + V2 + O
Keywords: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020
Example: The result came out yesterday at 10 AM.

2. Past Continuous → S + was/were + V1+ing + O
Keywords: while, when, at 5 PM yesterday
Example: I was sleeping when the result notification popped up.

3. Past Perfect → S + had + V3 + O
Keywords: before, after, already, by the time
Example: By the time I woke up, my friends had already checked their marks.

4. Past Perfect Continuous → S + had + been + V1+ing + O
Keywords: for, since, before
Example: I had been revising Maths for two hours straight before I finally took a break.

content.en:
Future Tense (4 Types) — with real examples

1. Simple Future → S + will/shall + V1 + O
Keywords: tomorrow, next week, soon
Example: I will start the syllabus revision tomorrow, promise.

2. Future Continuous → S + will/shall + be + V1+ing + O
Keywords: at this time tomorrow, at 5 PM next Monday
Example: This time next week, we will be writing the actual board exam.

3. Future Perfect → S + will/shall + have + V3 + O
Keywords: by next week, by the time, before 2027
Example: By the time boards start, I will have finished all 8 chapters of Section B.

4. Future Perfect Continuous → S + will/shall + have + been + V1+ing + O
Keywords: for two hours by then, by next year
Example: By March, I will have been studying this app's Grammar lessons for six months straight.

content.en:
🥊 Confusion Buster — The 3 Pairs That Cost the Most Marks

PAIR 1: Simple Past vs Present Perfect
• Ask: "Is there an exact time mentioned?" → YES = Simple Past | NO (or 'ever since') = Present Perfect
• ❌ "I have watched that movie yesterday." (has a time word 'yesterday')
• ✅ "I watched that movie yesterday." OR "I have watched that movie." (no time given)

PAIR 2: Present Continuous vs Present Perfect Continuous
• Ask: "Did this start recently and it's ONLY about right now?" → Present Continuous | "Has this been going on for a while, started earlier?" → Present Perfect Continuous
• Present Continuous: "I am doing my homework." (just describing now, no sense of duration)
• Present Perfect Continuous: "I have been doing my homework for an hour." (duration matters — since when/how long)

PAIR 3: Past Simple vs Past Perfect
• Ask: "Are there TWO past actions and I need to show which happened FIRST?" → the earlier one gets Past Perfect, the later one stays Simple Past
• "When I reached [later action] the station, the train had already left [earlier action]."
• If there's only ONE past action, just use Simple Past — don't force Past Perfect where it isn't needed.
content.hi:
🥊 Confusion Buster — Ye 3 Pairs Sabse Zyada Marks Katte Hain

PAIR 1: Simple Past vs Present Perfect
• Poocho: "Kya exact time mention hai?" → HAAN = Simple Past | NAHI (ya 'ever since') = Present Perfect
• ❌ "I have watched that movie yesterday." ('yesterday' ek time word hai)
• ✅ "I watched that movie yesterday." YA "I have watched that movie." (koi time nahi diya)

PAIR 2: Present Continuous vs Present Perfect Continuous
• Poocho: "Ye recently start hua hai aur sirf abhi ki baat hai?" → Present Continuous | "Ye kuch time se chal raha hai, pehle start hua tha?" → Present Perfect Continuous
• Present Continuous: "I am doing my homework." (bas abhi ki baat, duration ka sense nahi)
• Present Perfect Continuous: "I have been doing my homework for an hour." (duration matter karta hai — kab se/kitni der se)

PAIR 3: Past Simple vs Past Perfect
• Poocho: "Do past actions hain aur mujhe dikhana hai kaunsa PEHLE hua?" → jo pehle hua wo Past Perfect, jo baad mein hua wo Simple Past hi rahega
• "When I reached [baad wali action] the station, the train had already left [pehle wali action]."
• Agar sirf EK hi past action hai, to Simple Past hi use karo — bina zaroorat ke Past Perfect mat lagao.

content.en:
🔑 Golden Rules (Exam ke liye MUST)

Rule 1: Since vs For
• SINCE = point of time (since 2020, since morning)
• FOR = duration (for 2 hours, for 5 days)

Rule 2: Yet vs Already
• YET = negative/question (Has he come yet?)
• ALREADY = positive (He has already come.)

Rule 3: V1, V2, V3
• V1 = Simple Present, Future, after modals
• V2 = Simple Past only
• V3 = Perfect tenses, Passive voice

Rule 4: 'Since' ke saath hamesha Simple Past
• It has been raining since it started. (NOT 'since it has started')
